MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  LA VERNE
  Monday, April 5, 2021

1.  In order to minimize the spread of the COVID- 19 Virus, Governor Newsom issued an Executive Order that
  temporarily  suspends  requirements  of  the Brown Act.  The Council Chambers was closed to the public, La Verne
  City Council Members and members of the public attended this meeting telephonically, and the meeting was live
  streamed on the City' s website.

2.  A regular meeting of the La Verne City Council was called to order by Mayor Hepburn at 6: 30 p. m.

3.  Council  Members  present:  Mayor Tim Hepburn
  Mayor Pro Tem Robin Carder
  Council Member Muir Davis ( Appointed Mayor Pro Tem)
  Council Member Wendy Lau
  Council Member Rick Crosby

  Absent:  None.

  Advisory personnel  present:  City Manager Robert Russi
  Assistant to the City Manager JR Ranells
  City Attorney Robert L. Kress
  Assistant City Clerk Lupe Gaeta Estrella

4.  Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mayor Pro Tem Carder.

5.  Announcements  of  Upcoming  Mayor Hepburn called for any public announcements and waited for staff to
  Community  Events  check for any announcements via telephone communication.

  There was none.

6.  Consent Calendar  It was moved by Carder, seconded by Lau, and unanimously carried by roll call
  to accept, approve, or act on the Consent Calendar items.

  City Council  Minutes  C i y Council Minutes of March 15. 2021 received and filed.

  Alvarado.

  Extension of Car Show  Fxten  ion  of  Car  Show  Contract  for Old Town  La Verne -  The Old
  Contract for Old Town La Verne  Town La Verne Business Improvement District ( BID) is requesting the City
  Council consider a one- year extension to the contract for the two cars shows
  held in Old Town La Verne. While it is recognized the car shows may not occur
  due to State and County Health orders relating to COVID, the BID and
  promoter are asking for the extension to potentially make up for the shows
  which  did  not occur  in 2020 and 2021.
   Page 2
  City Council Minutes, Monday, April 5, 2021,

  Community Development Director Scherer and the Old Town La Verne
  Business Improvement District recommended that the City Council approve
  the proposed extension of the agreement with the promoter, Flying Deuces, to
  host car shows, if permitted,  until  April  of  2022. APPROVED  AS
  RECOMMENDED  BY STAFF.

  Rotation  of  Mayor Pro Tem  Rotation  of  Mayor  Pro Tem -  The City Council has followed a formal
  procedure for the rotation of the office of Mayor Pro Tem since 1993 and
  reaffirmed that policy annually. Attached is Resolution No, 20- 19 establishing
  the rotation policy of the office of Mayor Pro Tem.

  Assistant City Clerk Estrella recommended that the City Council appoint Muir
  Davis as Mayor Pro Tem who is next on the rotation list pursuant to Resolution
  No. 20- 19, for a one- year term, or until the second Council meeting of March of
  2022.  APPROVED AS RECOMMENDED BY STAFF.

7.  Amherst  Housing  City Attorney Kress reported that a resolution that should have been included
  Development, 2820 Amherst  was inadvertently left off the Agenda, Therefore, he recommended that public
  Street, Case  Nos. 17- 20PPR,  hearing be continued to the April 19, 2021.

  19- 20GPA,  18- 20TTM  Mayor Hepburn opened the public hearing and it was the consensus of the
  City Council to continue the matter to the April 19, 2021, Council meeting.

  Amherst Housinq Development, 2820 Amherst Street, Case Nos. 17-
  20PPR, 11- 20TR, 20- 20ZC, 109- 20SP, 19- 20GPA, 18- 20TTM - Request to
  construct 42 detached sinqle- familv homes.  The applicant, Matt Waken

  with MJW Investments, LLC, is proposing to develop 42 single- family homes at
  2820 Amherst Street( 8666- 021- 902) and a portion of the adjacent parcel,
  8666- 021- 904, both City owned properties. The properties are currently zoned
  PR3D and are designated Low Density Residential in the General Plan. The
  Planning Commission recommended by a 4- 0 vote that the City Council deny
  the request unless the density of the project is lowered, resulting in fewer
  homes. Staff and the Development  Review Committee ( DRC)  recommend

  approval to the City Council for Case Numbers 18- 20TTM, 20- 20ZC, 109-
  20SP, and 19- 20GPA, based on the staff report and the conditions of approval.

8.  Adoption  of the  Fire Code  of  the  City Engineer Milano reported on the proposed adoption of the Fire Code of
  Los Angeles County Code  the Los Angeles County Code Incorporating by Reference the 2019 Edition of
  Incorporating by Reference the  the California Fire Code with Certain Changes and Amendments. He stated
  2019 Edition  of the  California  that the County of Los Angeles on March 10, 2020 adopted Title 32— Fire
  Fire Code with Certain  Code of the Los Angeles County Code by incorporating by reference the 2019
  Changes  and  Amendments  Edition of the California Fire Code, with certain changes and amendments.
  The City of La Verne' s Fire Marshal and City Engineer have reviewed the
  changes made by the County of Los Angeles and are recommending
  additional changes specific to the City of La Verne. The code with the
  recommended changes establishes fire standards for the City of La Verne to
  promote the health and safety of the general public.

  Mayor Hepburn called for public comment on this matter and waited for staff to
  respond with any requests from the public via the webinar.

  There was  none.
   City Council Minutes, Monday, April 5, 2021,  Page 3

  It was moved by Davis, seconded by Lau, and unanimously carried by roll call
  to introduce by title, waive further reading and set the public hearing for
  Monday, April 19, 2021, for Ordinance No. 1101, adopting Title 32 - Fire
  Code of the Los Angeles County with the City of La Verne amendments.

9.  Public Comment  This was the time set aside for anyone wishing to address the City Council on
  items not listed in any other  place  on  the agenda.  Mayor Hepburn called for
  public comment and waited for staff to check for any public comment via the
  webinar.

  Richard  Bowen spoke via the webinar.

  To hear what was said during public comment, please visit the City' s website
  to view the archived Council meeting.

  One public comment received via email ( attached).

12.  Adjournment at 7: 30 p. m., in memory of City of La Verne Fleet Manager Bob Crawford. Bob passed away
  cancer. He was born on May 18, 1968, in Cleveland
  peacefully at the age of 52 after a valiant fight against
  Ohio  and  moved  to California  when  he  was  12.  His love of all things equipment related began with his dad,
  who was  a  truck  mechanic.  Bob graduated from Villa Park High School and then quickly earned a certificate in
  diesel and heavy truck repair leading to his first position as a fleet mechanic with the Fullerton School District in
  1991. After stops  outside  of  local government, Bob returned to the public sector as a Fleet Superintendent
  with  the  City  of  Burbank and as luck would have it, he was hired as the Fleet Manager in 2018 for the City of
  La Verne. Bob  was  a  knowledgeable,  respected,  and  incredibly well  liked  by all  at  the  City. Away from
  work,  Bob  enjoyed  spending time with his  family  and  riding bicycles as well as motorcycles. Bob is
  his wife Sandi of 26 years; finro  children,  Andrew and Alison. Bob will be truly missed by those that
  survived by
  have had the pleasure of being around him.
